text:
Ashwin: Heads up — sketching a new approach for API key/org rate limiting to handle fleet saturation. TL;DR: tiered degrade + redistributed active slots instead of strict per-key hard caps. want quick feedback. :wave:

Lina: curious — what do you mean by redistributed slots? sounds like stealing capacity from idle keys?

Ashwin: yeah — idea is to keep a global token pool per-pool (GPU rack / region) that feeds short-lived ‘active slots’ for in-flight requests. each org/key has a soft share (weighted) and a hard floor. when pool is saturated we proportionally reduce soft shares and allow short borrow windows for bursty keys.

Raj: how is this different from our current token-bucket + refill? seems similar to spare-capacity borrowing we discussed.

Ashwin: good q — current is purely per-key token-buckets with independent refill. this proposal centralizes admission at the pool level so we can enforce capacity-aligned admission. main differences:
- admission is aware of node saturation metrics (GPU occupancy / queue length)
- soft vs hard portions: soft can be scaled down under pressure, hard is protected for higher-tier customers
- short borrow windows are time-limited and reconciled to avoid long tail steal

Jordan: can you paste a tiny pseudo-config? helps to visualize.

Ashwin: sure — rough:
```
pool: us-west-2-gpu-a
pool_capacity_tokens: 1000  # maps roughly to concurrent slots
org_shares: {enterprise: 0.5, standard: 0.4, free: 0.1}
org_hard_floor: {enterprise: 300, standard: 50, free: 0}
borrow_window_ms: 5000  # short bursts allowed
adaptive_scale_thresholds: {gpu_util_crit: 0.92, queue_crit: 50} 
```

Lina: hmm, so if enterprise has hard_floor 300, it's guaranteed even under saturation. what about fairness when many enterprise keys are idle? will standard/free get starved?

Ashwin: that's where redistribution comes in. soft shares are computed from remaining pool after reserving all hard floors. if enterprise uses less than its floor, remaining capacity is redistributed per shares. if all enterprise are idle, more goes to standard/free.

Raj: how do we avoid oscillation where keys keep borrowing and then starving others repeatedly? sounds unstable.

Ashwin: we limit borrow frequency with cooldowns and track per-key short-term borrow rate. also we prefer redistributing by org (aggregate) not by individual key to smooth noise. decay windows are like 30s for borrow tracking.

Jordan: ops question — how do we tie this to real node signals? CPU/GPU util, ready queue depth, and avg latency? which signals are first-class?

Ashwin: primary triggers: GPU compute utilization (>crit threshold), scheduler queue length (>crit), and token refill pressure (pool tokens hitting near-zero). combination logic: if two+ triggers fire, we step degrade to next level (scale soft shares by 0.7, then 0.5...).

Lina: any concern about routing complexity? we currently route by org->pool simple mapping. if admission becomes global per-pool, latency for admission check must stay tiny.

Ashwin: agree. plan is to keep admission path local in edge proxies that cache pool state and do O(1) token checks. controllers push scaled share deltas to proxies every ~1s. checkout this micro-sequence:
1) metrics collector flags pool pressure
2) controller computes new soft-share multipliers
3) push to proxies via fast config channel (gossip or push)
4) proxies apply immediate admission changes; borrow/cooldown enforcement local

Raj: safe fallback if controller or push fails? we don't want proxies to revert to permissive behavior and explode.

Ashwin: default is conservative: on loss of control-plane signals, proxies fall back to last-known good multipliers and then step to a stricter multiplier after a watchdog timeout (10s). also enforce per-key hard floors locally always.

Jordan: what about metrics and billing accuracy? if we borrow across orgs, how do we attribute tokens?

Ashwin: attribute by actual served tokens — if standard borrowed unused enterprise capacity, billing records the origin org as usual. borrow just affects admission, not attribution. ops will see cross-org borrow logs for audits.

Lina: sounds promising. a couple of risks: (1) complexity in controllers, (2) ensuring proxy push latency is stable, (3) telemetry to debug weird allocation during incidents. we should prototype with one pool.

Ashwin: agreed. plan: prototype in one us-west-2-gpu-a staging pool for 2 weeks, add extensive event logs (borrow/grant/release) and a small dashboard showing allocated vs reserved vs used.

sre-bot: incident-note: created test pool 'staging-tiered-degrade-01' at 2150001300 for Ashwin. :white_check_mark:

Raj: ok let's do it. I'll own the proxy push code. Lina can own telemetry/dashboard. Ashwin will build controller and configs. Jordan pls help with node-level signals mapping.

Jordan: on it. will sketch mapping by EOD.

Lina: can we include a fail-safe to reject long-running low-priority jobs outright under severe pressure? prefer reject to indefinite queueing.

Ashwin: yes — that is part of the soft-degrade policy (hard reject for free tier when pool < 20% available). we'll document thresholds in the RFC draft.

Raj: cool. next steps: small RFC + proto in staging. I'll open a tracking ticket.

Ashwin: thanks team. will follow up with RFC link and config gist. :rocket:
